summary: Wei Lin works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Nanjing University and Peking University, Lin earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, University of Michigan, and Transylvania University.

Wei-Cheng Lin is a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. Lin served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill from circa 2008 to 2015 and took up a post at the University of Chicago in 2015.

Wei-jen Teng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Teng studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, University of Chicago, and Harvard University, completing a PhD supervised by Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Teng began teaching at Dharma Drum Institute circa 2012.
Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Shen taught at the University of Hong Kong and held a position at Renmin University of China from circa 2006 to 2015.
Weiru Guan is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University from circa 2008 to 2011, supervised by Yongdong Shi.

Wen-ling Jane specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jane completed a PhD at Columbia University by 2009 under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai is an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Hamburg, Kyoto University, and Peking University, where Mai earned a PhD. Mai has served as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, completing a PhD at Stanford University. Adamek held posts at Barnard College from circa 2001 to 2010 and at the University of Calgary as associate professor around 2014.

Wendy Doniger specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Radcliffe College, Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and the University of Oxford, Doniger served as the Mircea Eliade Distinguished Service Professor of the History of Religions at the University of Chicago (~1978–2018).

Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Duan studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts from circa 1940 to 1943 and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy from circa 1984 to 1998.

Wenjie Qin specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Qin completed a PhD at Harvard University circa 1997–2004 under doctoral supervisor Tu Weiming, also studying under Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.
Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna from 1962 to 1965. Abraham held an academic post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich in 2002.
Wes Borton works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied at East Carolina University, where Derek F. Maher was a teacher, and at the University of Michigan.

Whalen Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Lai studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD at Harvard University, later serving as an assistant professor at UIUC and professor of religious studies at UC Davis (~1976–2003).

Whitney Cox is an Indologist who studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago, working under Sheldon Pollock, Wendy Doniger, and others. Cox held a post at the University of Chicago around 2013.

Wilburn Hansen focuses on Japanology and religious studies. Hansen pursued a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder (~1996–1999) and studied at Stanford University (~2000–2006) under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar educated at Upper Canada College, the University of Toronto, and Princeton University. Smith served as a director at Harvard University from circa 1964 to 1973.

Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. Sellars held academic posts at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale University (1958–1963), and University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and Frederick William University Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. Deecke held teaching posts at Katharineum (1852–1855) and Ernestinenschule (1855–1870).

Wilhelm Geiger (1856–1943) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian studies, and linguistics. After doctoral studies at Erlangen under Friedrich von Spiegel, he held posts at Erlangen and later Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich as chair of Indology and Iranian studies (1886–1924).
